recipe.title: Start your pipeline
recipe.subtitle: Pick a starting point. You can still edit every field on the following steps.
recipe.blankBody: Empty form. Bring your own dumps and oracle; set every threshold yourself. Best for power users running on a new target.
recipe.gocryptfsBody: Loads the IMF paper's section 4.2 thresholds (variance ≥ 1500, 8-byte alignment, entropy ≥ 4.5) for the single-N brute-force pass, which stays exhaustive so it reports every hit, plus the published section 7 N-sweep (N = 1,3,5,10,15,20, stride 8), which carries its own settings and stops at the first verified key. Point it at
recipe.gocryptfsBodyTail: and upload the gocryptfs oracle on the next step to reproduce both verified hits.
recipe.saveLoadNote: Recipe save / load / share is planned for a later release; for now the two presets above cover the IMF demo and the blank starting point.

dumps.discoverEmpty: No dumps of the selected kinds were found in this directory.
dumps.discoverTruncated: Only the first {{count}} matches are listed — this is not the complete set. Pick a narrower folder or fewer kinds to see the rest.
dumps.pasteHint: A line that names a folder is scanned for the dumps inside it, exactly as Browse folder… does. Files are added as they are; a path that does not exist is refused.
dumps.pasteMoreFolders_one: {{paths}} is a folder too, and folders are scanned one at a time. It is still in the box — add these dumps first, then paste it again.
dumps.pasteMoreFolders_other: {{count}} more folders were pasted ({{paths}}), and folders are scanned one at a time. They are still in the box — add these dumps first, then paste them again.
dumps.referenceNote: Dump 1 is the reference: only its bytes are verified against the oracle. The others refine the variance filter, so make sure dump 1 comes from the same run as the oracle you configure next.

oracle.subtitlePrefix: The oracle is your decryption check. Upload a

pcap.uploadHint: Upload a capture of the same TLS session; the server parses its handshakes so you can pick which one to match.

pcap.fieldsHint: Field ids you can name instead of pasting hex — hand one to 'locate-key --pcap-field'. Only searchable fields make usable dump needles.
pcap.fieldsPickSession: This capture holds several sessions. Pick one above to see its fields — another session's field is a valid-looking needle from the wrong handshake.

thresholds.title: Configure thresholds
thresholds.subtitlePrefix: Tune the variance / alignment / entropy filter chain. Defaults come from the gocryptfs IMF case study; hover the
thresholds.exhaustiveLabel: Exhaustive (try every candidate even after the first hit)
thresholds.emitEnableLabel: Emit a Volatility 3 plugin from the best hit
thresholds.emitHint: Writes emit_plugin/<name>.py plus a field map alongside the run's other artifacts, and fills the Plugin tab on the results screen. Leave this off and no plugin is produced.
thresholds.nsweepEnableLabel: Run the N-sweep harness and build the interactive report
thresholds.nsweepHint: Re-folds a fresh consensus at every N and writes nsweep/report.json, .html and .md, which fills the Report tab on the results screen. Costs one full consensus + reduce + verify pass per N.
thresholds.nsweepPcapUnavailable: The N-sweep harness re-runs the oracle at every N and needs an uploaded oracle file, so it is unavailable on a pcap-oracle run.
thresholds.nsweepPcapHint: Re-folds a fresh consensus at every N and re-verifies against your capture through the same pcap oracle the brute-force stage uses. Costs one full consensus + reduce + verify pass per N.
thresholds.nsweepFirstHitLabel: Stop at the first verified key (the sweep's own --first-hit)
thresholds.nsweepGridHint: Stride and first-hit size the sweep's OWN candidate grid. The sweep does not inherit them from the brute-force settings above, so the two can disagree: the published gocryptfs run swept at stride 8 and stopped at the first verified key. Key size is fixed at 32 bytes on both paths and has no control.
thresholds.noOracleError: No oracle selected. Go back to the Oracle step.
thresholds.noDumpsError: No dump paths provided. Go back to the Dumps step.

fields.minVarianceHelp: Per-byte variance threshold. Higher values keep only very volatile bytes; in the IMF paper 1500 separated real crypto material from noise at N≥20.
fields.alignmentHelp: Byte alignment the key must land on. Go's allocator places keys on 8-byte boundaries; most allocators use 8 or 16.
fields.blockSizeHelp: Window the aligned density filter scores. 32 bytes fits a single AES-256 key; wider windows score pairs of adjacent keys.
fields.densityHelp: Minimum survivor fraction inside an aligned block before it's kept. 0.5 means half the bytes in the window must already be candidates.
fields.entropyWinHelp: Sliding-window size for Shannon entropy in bytes. Must be larger than the entropy threshold in bits, raised to 2.
fields.entropyMinHelp: Minimum Shannon entropy (bits) a window must hit. Cryptographic keys saturate near log2(window); keep this ≤ log2(window).
fields.minRegionHelp: Smallest contiguous region the reducer will emit. Regions shorter than this are dropped before brute-force.
fields.strideHelp: Candidate iteration step. Defaults to 1, which walks every offset for full coverage. Raising it is faster but only tests offsets that are multiples of the stride, so an unaligned secret can never be found.
fields.jobsHelp: Worker processes for the brute-force sweep. 0 (the default) auto-selects: a large exhaustive sweep runs on a small pool, while a short sweep or a first-hit run stays serial so the reported candidate count stays reproducible. Set 1 to force serial (easiest debugging), or any higher number to pin the worker count. MemDiver v1 caps concurrent pipelines at 1, so the chosen count is the whole CPU footprint.
fields.topKHelp: When no hit is found, how many highest-variance regions to report. Zero to disable the fallback.
fields.pluginNameHelp: Module name for the emitted Volatility 3 plugin. Becomes the artifact filename (<name>.py) and the generated plugin class, so keep it a valid Python identifier.
fields.minStaticRatioHelp: Minimum fraction of a hit's neighborhood that must classify as static before a signature is emitted. 0.3 (the default) demands that under a third of the surrounding bytes be stable; raise it to emit only tightly-framed structures.
fields.nValuesHelp: Comma-separated dump counts to sweep, e.g. 1,3,5,10. Each N re-folds a fresh consensus over that many dumps, so the list length multiplies the run time. The default ladder is clamped to the number of dumps you selected.
fields.nsweepStrideHelp: Candidate iteration step for the sweep only, independent of the brute-force stride above. 1 walks every offset for full coverage; raising it is faster but only tests offsets that are multiples of the stride, so an unaligned secret can never be found. The published gocryptfs run used 8.

dryRun.smokeTest_one: Smoke test the oracle on {{count}} sample before committing to a full sweep.
dryRun.smokeTest_other: Smoke test the oracle on {{count}} samples before committing to a full sweep.
dryRun.testTitle: Verify the oracle loads and runs before committing to a full sweep
dryRun.legendNote: one control should pass, decoys should fail
dryRun.unknownError: the server refused the request without giving a reason
dryRun.composedNote: Samples are composed on the server from your first dump: one known-good key as a positive control, plus decoys read from real dump bytes.
dryRun.noDumps: Pick at least one dump on the previous step — the smoke test reads its samples out of the first one.

verdict.discriminates: This oracle discriminates: it accepted the known-good key and rejected the decoys. Safe to run a full sweep.
verdict.never_accepts: This oracle never accepts: it rejected the known-good key, so a full sweep would report no hits no matter what is in the dump.
verdict.accepts_noise: This oracle accepts noise: it said yes to arbitrary dump bytes, so a full sweep would report false hits.
verdict.no_positive_control: Half-tested: the decoys were rejected, but no known-good key was available, so nothing proved this oracle can ever say yes.
verdict.inconclusive: Inconclusive: this run did not produce enough clean signal to judge the oracle — check the errors below.

dryRun.positiveSelfTestNote: The control key comes from this dataset's recorded answer key (meta.json). It is a self-test of the oracle, not a pipeline finding — nothing was searched for here.
dryRun.positiveAbsentNoReason: The server did not say why.
dryRun.negativesSource: Decoys read from {{name}} ({{view}} view), {{keySize}} bytes each.
dryRun.negativesSourceNone: No dump could be opened, so no decoys were tested.
dryRun.lowEntropyNote_one: {{count}} decoy came from a low-entropy region — an easy rejection that flatters the result.
dryRun.lowEntropyNote_other: {{count}} decoys came from low-entropy regions — easy rejections that flatter the result.

examples.intro: Pick a bundled template to inspect its shape. Examples are read-only — copy one into your own
examples.introTail: tab to actually run a pipeline.
examples.useIntro: Or use one as it ships: “Use this example” registers the bundled file on the server so it becomes a runnable oracle — a Shape 2 example asks for its config first.
examples.configHint: This oracle is built from a config. Anything MemDiver could work out from the dumps you picked is filled in below; an empty row shows the example's own template as a hint — that text is not a path on this machine, so answer it before loading.
examples.configEmptyHint: This example ships no config template. Add the keys its build_oracle(cfg) expects, or load it unarmed and arm it from the Upload tab.
examples.unfilledNote: The example's template only hints at this value:
examples.unfilledBlock: Fill in {{keys}} first — the example's template value is a hint, not a file on this machine, and the server refuses it.
examples.cipherMismatch: This example cannot verify the selected dumps: {{reason}} Arming it would sweep every candidate to false and read as “key not found”.
examples.referenceChanged: The values below were derived from {{run}}, which is no longer the first selected dump. Each run has its own master key, so clear the field and let it re-derive before arming.
examples.loaded: Loaded {{filename}} — arm it from the Upload tab to run it.
examples.loadedUnarmed: Loaded {{filename}} unarmed — arm it from the Upload tab to run it.
examples.armed: Loaded and armed {{filename}} — you can continue.
examples.unknownError: the server refused the request without giving a reason

shape.introMid: is a short Python file you write that returns
shape.introTail: for everything else. Memdiver's pipeline hands it each surviving candidate from the search-reduce chain and reports the ones that pass. The server never sees the plaintext; you decide what "verified" means for your protocol.
shape.twoShapesPrefix: Two shapes are supported; pick Shape 1 for simple cases and Shape 2 when
shape.twoShapesTail: needs to cache work (like a KDF output or an open socket) between calls.
shape.securityNotePrefix: Memdiver refuses to load oracles from world-writable files, purges any stale
shape.securityNoteMid: next to the source, and requires an explicit "Arm oracle" step that re-hashes the file on disk before the pipeline will run it. See

upload.armTitle: Confirm sha256 and mark this oracle safe to execute
upload.consentBody: An oracle is Python you supply, and MemDiver runs it in this server's process to test every surviving key candidate. Enable this only for code you wrote or have read.
upload.consentStorage: Uploads will be stored in {{path}}. The directory is created for your user only (mode 0700) and each oracle file is written read-write to you alone (0600).
